items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: Then you had Glover Compton and all these fellows -- they had them from all around.

ctx.x: Opal Cooper, I think he was from Chicago. Then you had Glover Compton and all these fellows -- they had them from all around. They had a bunch of fellows who come out from Spain. They had their Spanish women but a boy named Chase, he come from Washington and one man named Mufflejaws Mars, he come from Washington, D. C. and sure, they was there too, and we would all meet Arthur Laniers also, then you had one fellow who was a jazz violin player named Juice Wilson. He was a violin player, I mean

he was a champ. He stayed in Algeria but he stayed too long. He lost all his finger on the fiddle but he played saxophone. He was something special. See, what happened, the guy had stayed -- he went over there as a young man with a show or something, and he stayed and then he didn't care about keeping up on his instrument. He became of the country where he lived and then you had Englishmen coming over --
